clue.text: It was felt to provide cover for du Maurier's heroine

definitions.text: It was felt to provide cover
definitions.meaning: a soft felt hat with a dented crown, worn to cover the head
the title character of George du Maurier's 1894 novel about an artist's model in Paris

explanation.surface: A coy remark that something was meant to shield a novelist's leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' looks like a past tense of feel, but it is the fabric the hat is made of; the hat took its name from the novel's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: This felt hat is named after the heroine because one was worn in the stage version of the novel.

clue.text: Journey north quite freely, being the E bleeding controller!

parts.note: a tour is a journey
N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: taken freely, the letters are allowed to fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Travelling north without restraint as a way of stemming the flow of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight band applied to a limb stops severe bleeding, so it controls blood loss.

clue.text: Detached territory named after Langerhans?

definitions.meaning: a small island, a scrap of land cut off by water
the ... of Langerhans are cell clusters in the pancreas named after the German anatomist

explanation.surface: A remote piece of land named in honour of a man called Langerhans.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the pancreatic cell clusters known by the anatomist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is a piece of land detached from the mainland, and the pancreatic clusters bear the same name.

clue.text: 1950s youth caught breaking out of prison with hammer

parts.note: to beat is to hammer

indicators.note: the cricket letter escapes, so it is removed from the jail word

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A young man of the fifties is arrested after a jailbreak with a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out of' leaves NIK once the cricket letter escapes the jail slang; '1950s youth' points to the Beat Generation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beat Generation's young followers of the late 1950s were nicknamed after it, a period label for a youth.

clue.text: Location of something nasty discarded by golf club?

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club
shed means cast off or discarded

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant thrown out by members of a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something nasty in the woodshed' is the famous half-glimpsed horror in Stella Gibbons's comic novel Cold Comfort Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Cold Comfort Farm puts the nasty thing in an outbuilding for storing firewood.

clue.text: One may be tall if demanding firm discipline

definitions.meaning: a 'tall' one is a demand that is hard to meet
control or discipline, as in keeping a class in good behaviour

explanation.surface: A tall person may insist on strict control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tall' suggests height, but it belongs to the idiom for a hard-to-meet demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for an excessive demand, and the word also means discipline or control.

clue.text: Entertainer's daughter has solution? Not with university intervening

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the entertainer alone

indicators.note: the university letter comes between the remaining letters
the letter for with is to be left out of the next word

parts.note: an answer is a solution

explanation.surface: A performer's daughter has the answer, but not with a college involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not with' drops W (the usual abbreviation for with) from ANSWER, leaving ANSER; 'intervening' puts U into it to make ANSEUR, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: A male ballet dancer is a stage performer, so an entertainer.

clue.text: Command vessel, being at top of 24

parts.note: to head is to command or lead
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: An order about a ship that ends up topping the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is BILL, so the definition is someone at the top of the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The star act whose name is billed first on a programme is described as headlining it.

clue.text: Swan-upping? It's so dull

indicators.note: in a down clue, upping means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Swan of Avon is Shakespeare, the Bard

explanation.surface: The annual counting of the Thames swans is a tedious affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Swan-upping is the annual marking of swans on the Thames; here 'upping' turns BARD round, the Swan of Avon being Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab is a direct synonym for dull, lacking colour or interest.

clue.text: Free soul? None freer

indicators.note: the letters are set freer, loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A free spirit is as unconstrained as anyone could be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freer' rearranges SOUL and NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloosen is to loosen or set free, a verb sense of free.

clue.text: In lacking guidance, English composer is ill-educated

indicators.note: these letters are placed in the word for lacking guidance

parts.note: unled means not led, lacking guidance
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: Without proper tuition, an English composer is poorly schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne is the English composer of Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Unlearned describes someone without learning, a synonym for ill-educated.

clue.text: Finally learn a poem about an antelope

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word learn
about turns the following letters round

parts.note: a lay is a narrative poem or song

explanation.surface: Learn a poem at last about an African antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A and LAY round to YALA, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Japanese drama award given to close relative? No way

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese masked drama
a Tony is an American theatre award
'our Nelly' in northern English usage is one's own sister Nelly, a close relative

explanation.surface: A theatre prize presented to a family member for Japanese drama is out of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern English speech 'our' before a name marks a family member, so 'our Nelly' is a close relative. The whole phrase is British slang for an emphatic refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming-slang exclamation is an emphatic refusal, equivalent to saying certainly not.

clue.text: Reportedly rejected from start to finish

indicators.note: reportedly means what follows is heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: threw out means rejected

explanation.surface: A report of something turned down all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals that THREW OUT, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting from start to finish lasts all the way through, the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: Living in the past one's dismissed for a phoney

indicators.note: the letter for one is sent off and replaced by the letter a

parts.note: quick meant alive in older English, as in 'the quick and the dead'

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the past is sacked for being a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is I and 'a' is A: I in QUICK is dismissed for A. 'in the past' marks quick as an old word for living.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack is a fraudulent pretender, especially to medical skill, so a phoney.

clue.text: Wilberforce achieved it, changing oil in boat

indicators.note: changing alters the order of these letters

explanation.surface: An anti-slavery campaigner managed something while altering oil in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges OIL, IN and BOAT. William Wilberforce led the campaign that ended Britain's slave trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilberforce's achievement was ending the slave trade, so the definition describes its abolishing.

clue.text: Small local office under overhanging part of tree

parts.note: sub is the Latin prefix meaning under
a branch is a limb of a tree that can overhang

explanation.surface: A tiny office sits beneath a branch reaching out over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor local outpost of a bank or firm is a smaller office below a branch.

clue.text: Worker of abstemious habit keeping animal in plant

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: keeping means holding the animal inside

parts.note: TT means teetotal, abstemious with drink
roo is short for kangaroo

explanation.surface: A teetotal labourer keeps a creature inside a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a vegetable plant grown for its red root.

clue.text: The Spanish formerly possessed that French way with words

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

indicators.note: possessed means holding the French word inside

parts.note: once means formerly
que is French for 'that'

explanation.surface: The Spanish once had a French gift for speaking well.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, persuasive speaking is a way with words, a description of oratorical skill.

clue.text: Suffer subject to influence of crack

parts.note: under means subject to, as in under the influence
a crack is an attempt, a go

explanation.surface: Endure being under the sway of something breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo hardship is to experience or suffer it.

clue.text: Sign right in centre of Spanish port

indicators.note: the right letter is placed in the middle of the port's name

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain

explanation.surface: A signal right in the middle of a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is a sign of the zodiac, the Virgin.

clue.text: Old way Sister gets involved covering church organs

indicators.note: gets involved means it is placed within the old road

parts.note: via is the Latin word for a road, as in Roman roads

indicators.note: covering means the sister letters go round the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun goes the old way, wrapped up in parish affairs and church music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' and 'gets involved' build SCER and put it into the old road; 'organs' looks like church music but means body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The viscera are the internal organs of the body, especially in the abdomen.

clue.text: Light sauce? It's the spin doctor's speciality

parts.note: a light is a window pane
dressing is a sauce, as for salad

explanation.surface: A thin sauce is the specialty of a political media adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for a thin sauce, but it is a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenting something to look better than it is, as a spin doctor does, is putting on a showy front.

clue.text: It may cause division in the club

definitions.meaning: a tapered block driven in to split things apart

explanation.surface: Something that might split the members of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a rift among members; the second sense is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapered block forces things apart, and the same word names a lofted golf club.

clue.text: Woman with husband like Wexford

parts.note: Iris is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman with her husband has something of an Irish county about her.
explanation.walkthrough: Wexford is a county in south-east Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Wexford is in Ireland, so something like it is from that country.

clue.text: The fellow one settles with in America?

definitions.meaning: a man's name, short for William
in the US a banknote is called by this word, so it is what you pay with

explanation.surface: A man in the US with whom one squares accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: In America a banknote takes this name, so it is something one settles a debt with.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common man's name, and American English uses it for a paper banknote.

clue.text: Here in France a monarch is comparatively aloof

parts.note: ici is French for 'here'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a monarch

explanation.surface: In France a king is rather standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy means coldly aloof, so the comparative is more distant in manner.

clue.text: Book beginning of month in cathedral

indicators.note: the date is placed inside the word for cathedral

parts.note: duomo is the Italian word for a cathedral
Dec I, the first of December, is the start of a month

explanation.surface: A volume opened at the start of the month in a great church.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman-style dating: Dec I is the first day of December, so the start of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A duodecimo is a book size made by folding sheets into twelve leaves, so a book.

clue.text: Recluse crossing river is a British citizen

indicators.note: crossing means straddling the river, which sits inside

parts.note: a loner is a recluse
the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A hermit wading across a river is a British subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of the British capital is one kind of British citizen.

clue.text: Virtuous person carrying long bag

indicators.note: carrying means holding the longing inside

parts.note: ST, saint, is a virtuous person
to long is to ache, yearn

explanation.surface: A good person holds a long bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed bag or packet.
